items.title: An auto-associated ring annihilates every proper finitely generated ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma derives the annihilator property (P) from auto-associatedness, and the proof is a 7-line argument that produces the annihilator explicitly. From the defining element of an auto-associated ring, which is killed by a power of every element of the maximal ideal, it deduces that this element lies in the kernel of the map to the product of the localisations at the generators of the given ideal, and then applies a criterion of the Algebra chapter which turns that membership into a nonzero annihilator of the whole ideal. The two steps — the production of the element and the covering criterion — are each a single displayed computation.
